More detailed information on the specific method used by each region is provided in Appendix B. Figure 3. Summary of cost allocation methods used in each RTO/ISO for different project types In comparison of the cost allocation methods used by different regions, several trends emerge. 1. The costs for local projects are allocated primarily using license plate approaches. Costs for these projects are allocated to the local pricing zone in which the project is being built (i.e., SPP, PJM, MISO) or to the local transmission owner (i.e., CAISO, NYISO, ISO-NE). The philosophy behind these approaches is that local projects will have localized benefits and should not be paid for by the broader planning region. Generator interconnection projects are almost exclusively paid for by direct assignment to the interconnecting generator. In all regions, except ERCOT and MISO, transmission upgrades to meet generator interconnection requests are fully cost allocated to the interconnecting customer. In MISO, the costs for interconnection projects below 345 kilovolts (kV) are allocated to the interconnecting generator. At or above 345 kV, 90% of costs are assigned to the generator, and 10% are allocated across the region based on usage. This approach assumes high-voltage lines provide broader benefits across the region, not just to the interconnecting customer. In ERCOT, interconnecting generation customers pay a limited interconnection cost to cover certain direct costs of connecting to the transmission system, and the remaining costs are passed to customers based on usage (Wilson et al. 2024). 3.
